business_model.claim: Brandywine Realty Trust is a self-administered, self-managed REIT that acquires, develops, redevelops, owns, manages, and operates office, life science/lab, residential, and mixed-use properties.
quotes: We are a self-administered and self-managed real estate investment trust (“REIT”) engaged in the acquisition, development, redevelopment, ownership, management, and operation of a portfolio of office, life science/lab, residential and mixed-use properties.

business_model.claim: The company generates cash and revenue primarily from property space leases, and to a lesser extent from third-party property management and development/redevelopment, unconsolidated real estate ventures, and asset sales.
quotes: We generate cash and revenue from leases of space at our Properties and, to a lesser extent, from the management and development/redevelopment of properties owned by third parties (primarily unconsolidated real estate ventures) and from investments in the unconsolidated real estate ventures.

We also generate cash through sales of assets, including assets that we do not view as core to our business plan, either because of location or expected growth potential, and assets that are commanding premium prices from third-party investors.

business_model.claim: The company operates and manages properties across Philadelphia CBD, Pennsylvania Suburbs, Austin, Texas, and Other geographic segments, plus a corporate support group.
quotes: During the nine months ended September 30, 2026, we owned and managed properties within four segments: (1) Philadelphia CBD, (2) Pennsylvania Suburbs, (3) Austin, Texas, and (4) Other.
The Philadelphia CBD segment includes properties located in the City of Philadelphia, Pennsylvania.
The Pennsylvania Suburbs segment includes properties in Chester, Delaware and Montgomery counties in the Philadelphia suburbs.
The Austin, Texas segment includes properties in the City of Austin, Texas.
The Other segment includes properties located in Northern Virginia, Washington, D.C., Southern Maryland, Camden County, New Jersey and New Castle County, Delaware.

In addition to the four segments, our corporate group is responsible for cash and investment management, development/redevelopment of certain real estate properties during the construction period, and certain other general support functions.

competitive_position.claim: Competing real estate developers and operators threaten Brandywine because some possess greater financial resources, better contractor and supplier pricing, faster lower-cost construction, and higher-vacancy space offered at lower rents or larger concessions.
quotes: We face significant competition from other real estate developers.
Some of these competitors may have significantly greater financial resources than we have.
These entities also may have more favorable relationships and pricing with suppliers and contractors and may complete construction projects sooner and at lower costs than we are able.

In addition, some of our competitors may be willing (e.g., because their properties may have vacancy rates higher than those for our properties) to make space available at lower rental rates or with higher tenant concession percentages than available space in our properties.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the 2025 Form 10-K Item 1 Competition section.
competitive_position.claim: Competition from domestic and foreign financial institutions, other REITs, pension funds, life insurers, and private investors can raise acquisition costs, restrict access to private deals, and depress disposition proceeds.
quotes: We also face competition when attempting to acquire, sell or develop real estate, including competition from domestic and foreign financial institutions, other REITs, life insurance companies, pension funds, partnerships and individual investors.
Our competitors may be able to pay higher property acquisition prices, may have private access to opportunities not available to us and otherwise may be in a better position to acquire a property.

Similarly, competition with sellers of similar properties to locate suitable purchasers may result in us receiving lower proceeds from a sale or in us not being able to dispose of a property at a time of our choosing due to the lack of an acceptable return.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the 2025 Form 10-K Item 1A Risk Factors and Q3 2026 Form 10-Q MD&A.
competitive_position.claim: Lease expirations, early termination rights, rent concessions, renovation demands, and tenant financial distress or bankruptcy threaten rental revenue and cash flow stability.
quotes: If tenants do not renew their leases upon expiration, we may be unable to re-lease the space.

Even if the tenants do renew their leases or if we can re-lease the space, the terms of renewal or re-leasing (including the cost of required renovations) may be less favorable than the current lease terms.

Periodically, our tenants experience financial difficulties, including bankruptcy, insolvency or a general downturn in their business, and these difficulties may have an adverse effect on our cash flow, results of operations, financial condition and ability to make distributions to our shareholders.

As a result, and as part of customary lease negotiations, we are often required to provide rent concessions or abatements, incur charges for tenant improvements and other inducements, including early termination rights or potential below market renewal options, all of which impact, in varying degrees, annualized rents.
